figures.alt: Compact half-bath rough-in beneath stairs with framed walls, plumbing locations, and protected floor
figures.caption: Even a compact powder-room addition depends on usable clearances, drainage, water supply, ventilation, framing, finishes, permit requirements, and access for the construction work.

figures.alt: Bathroom vanity installation layout with cabinet positioning, plumbing stub-outs, electrical boxes, and level floor protection
figures.caption: A full bath adds a denser group of decisions: shower or tub, vanity, lighting, ventilation, waterproofing, tile, plumbing, electrical work, and the connection to the existing house.

figures.alt: Master bathroom shower under construction with continuous waterproofing membrane, recessed niche, drain, and carefully prepared wall framing
figures.caption: Larger primary-bath additions carry more finish and coordination risk. The water-managed shower assembly, fixtures, layout, services, and details need to be included before a cost range is meaningful.
